title: How to Win Your Fantasy League (Picks 5-8)
sourceType: YouTube transcript supplied by the user
sourceContext: The example mock used Sleeper pricing. Player timing is therefore translated through the site's current ESPN/full-PPR ADP rather than copied as a hard round rule.
usage: Soft draft-construction and opportunity-cost prior. Current availability, projections, injury status, league rules, ADP, tier breaks, and personal Avoid flags retain priority.
principles: Treat pick 5 as a conditional RB-or-WR fork; take a clear top-four faller when one reaches the slot.
A Round 1 wide receiver increases the urgency to secure a viable running back in Round 2 before the position thins.
A Round 1 running back preserves flexibility to take the best RB or WR value in Round 2.
Prefer a five-round full house of three RB and two WR or three WR and two RB, with a mild preference for the 3 RB / 2 WR version.
A 2 RB / 2 WR / 1 TE opening is acceptable when an elite tight end falls materially below market price.
Do not force quarterback or tight end early. Consider them when a genuine tier or ADP discount appears, otherwise build RB and WR first.
Robust RB and zero-RB paths are board-dependent exceptions, not default instructions.
Later rounds should balance upside backs and receivers with stable weekly volume, then fill quarterback and tight end at value.

pickFiveMockExample.lesson: Open with an elite, high-volume receiver when the top running backs are gone.
Respond to a WR opening by securing an RB before the next tier is exhausted.
Take a high-volume receiver who falls below the analyst's valuation.
Break the RB/WR build only for a meaningful elite-TE value.
Restore positional balance with an upside RB2 candidate.
Add receiver upside after the starting core is stable.
Use a mid-round bench slot on contingent running-back upside when healthy and available.
Fill quarterback after the RB/WR core when a viable starter remains.
Close the example with a late receiver swing.

modelApplication.roundOne: Small named-player and RB/WR bonuses; early QB/TE is penalized unless the market discount is exceptional.
modelApplication.roundTwoResponse: A WR opener creates a strong RB need bonus. An RB opener keeps RB and WR nearly neutral.
modelApplication.roundFiveCheckpoint: The engine rewards 3/2 RB-WR builds and permits 2/2 plus TE when the TE was a value.
modelApplication.quarterbackAndTightEnd: Early selections require a visible ADP/tier discount; unfilled positions gain urgency from Round 9 onward.
modelApplication.examplePlayers: The ten-round mock provides small round-local priors only; it never guarantees availability or forces a selection.
